components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Dominant local action for tutor progress or committed user action.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { height: 44px; padding: 0 16px; border-radius: 6px; border: 1px solid color-mix(in oklab, #b9975b 70%, #d5cfc4); background: #b9975b; color: #1e1c18; font: 600 0.95rem/1 Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif; transition: background-color 140ms cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1), box-shadow 140ms cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: color-mix(in oklab, #b9975b 88%, #fdfbf8); box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.06); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid color-mix(in oklab, #b9975b 55%, transparent); outline-offset: 2px; }

narrative.overview: Dialogia is a product surface for private learning, model exploration, and careful thought. Its visual system should feel like sitting at a well-kept study desk: warm paper, clear annotations, quiet tools, and a tutor who knows when to step forward.
keyCharacteristics: Editorial surfaces that privilege reading and sustained attention.
Quiet power: advanced controls remain discoverable but visually secondary.
Tutor-first hierarchy: progress, feedback, and next steps are clearer than provider machinery.
Warm restraint: gold and plum accents are used as signals, not decoration.
Trust-preserving states for privacy, ZDR, local storage, and provider routing.

rules.name: The Accent Rarity Rule
rules.body: Gold and plum should not compete. Gold means tutor/action/progress; plum means model capability or secondary intelligence.

rules.name: The Voice Split Rule
rules.body: Tutor and assistant prose is serif. Controls and user-authored interactive surfaces are sans.

rules.name: The Paper Stack Rule
rules.body: Use borders and tonal changes first. Add shadow only when a surface has a reason to sit above another surface.

dos: Do make tutor mode feel central.
Do keep advanced controls close but quiet.
Do use Surface Paper, Muted Vellum, Warm Rule, and warm shadows to create reading comfort.
Do maintain strong focus states, keyboard access, reduced-motion fallbacks, and mobile touch targets near 44px.
Do interpret user text generously in UX copy.
donts: Don't make Dialogia feel like a generic AI chat wrapper.
Don't use purple-gradient startup UI, neon/cyberpunk cues, or decorative glassmorphism.
Don't make tutor mode feel like gamified noise or analytics theater.
Don't use a border-left or border-right thicker than 1px as a colored accent on cards, callouts, tutor panels, or alerts.
Don't use gradient text, decorative metric blocks, identical card grids, or modal-first flows.
Don't let power-user controls become a cockpit.
